what: Move prismis's LLM services into its own config.toml ([services.<name>] with base_url, model, api_key = "env:NAME"), read provider keys only from the environment, remove apiconf and every read of ~/.config/llm-core/services.toml outside migrate-config, make a first run's default config (OpenRouter, openai/gpt-5.4-nano, OPENROUTER_API_KEY) reach an LLM, and migrate existing installs.
why: Design: docs/work/self-contained-llm-config/design.md. Found on real use (2026-10-07): a fresh install following the README never reaches an LLM, because the daemon reads llm-core's services.toml and apiconf, neither of which anything creates, and ignores the key the docs ask for. After merge, cerebro is migrated and bridged to the operator's apiconf store with `apiconf env prismis` at launch, outside the lane.

criteria.given: an empty XDG config home and the local LLM stub
criteria.when: the daemon's first run writes the default config, the test points [services.openrouter] base_url at the stub, sets OPENROUTER_API_KEY, and runs `prismis-daemon verify`'s checks
criteria.then: it fails if the LLM check fails or anything is read from ~/.config/llm-core/ or ~/.config/apiconf/; otherwise the light service check passes, and the same walk run against the pre-change code fails on the missing services.toml

criteria.given: a config.toml service whose api_key is env:NAME with NAME unset, one whose api_key is a literal value, and one with no api_key
criteria.when: each is resolved for a call
criteria.then: it fails if the unset or literal one resolves, or the keyless one does not; otherwise the first two raise an error naming the service and the variable, and the keyless one calls without a key

criteria.when: `grep -rn apiconf` and `grep -rn llm-core` run over daemon/src, cli/src, daemon/pyproject.toml and daemon/uv.lock
criteria.then: it fails if apiconf appears anywhere or llm-core's path appears outside migrate-config and its tests; otherwise neither does

criteria.given: a config home shaped like cerebro's: config.toml naming prismis-light, prismis-deep and prismis-kind (decisions adapter), a services.toml defining them with key names, and an apiconf config.toml mapping those keys to provider openrouter with values
criteria.then: it fails if any [services.*] table is missing or differs from its source, if api_key is not env:OPENROUTER_API_KEY, if any key value appears in a file it wrote, if no timestamped backup exists, or if the second run changes anything; otherwise config.toml gains the three tables and keeps its comments

criteria.given: a config whose [llm] still uses the pre-llm-core provider format
criteria.then: it fails if it writes services.toml or apiconf's file, or copies a key value anywhere; otherwise config.toml gains [services.prismis-<provider>] with api_key = env:<VAR>

criteria.given: the README Quick Start, the .env template written by make install-config and the first-run next-steps text
criteria.then: it fails if any names a key variable or file the code does not read; otherwise all three name OPENROUTER_API_KEY and ~/.config/prismis/.env
it fails on any failing check; otherwise its last line is `verify: PASS`

outOfScope: prismis no longer follows edits to services.toml; its services live in its own config.toml after migration, and the prismis-* entries left in services.toml are inert for prismis.
Keys no longer come from apiconf directly; the operator's store reaches prismis only through the environment, so the apiconf CLI and an app profile are needed on each host that runs the daemon.
A newcomer default on OpenRouter means an OpenAI-only user edits base_url and model (documented in the README) rather than getting OpenAI by default.
stakes: From an empty config home, the first run, then setting OPENROUTER_API_KEY, then `prismis-daemon verify` reaches a passing LLM check; the test runs this path against the local LLM stub with only base_url pointed at the stub.
No prismis code path reads ~/.config/llm-core/services.toml except migrate-config, and apiconf is absent from daemon/pyproject.toml, uv.lock and every import.

Every LLM provider key comes from an environment variable named by `env:NAME` in a [services.*] api_key; a literal api_key value and a missing variable each fail with an error naming the service and the variable. prismis's own [api]/[remote] REST key is unchanged.
A service with no api_key works keyless.

migrate-config on cerebro's current config produces [services.prismis-light], [services.prismis-deep] and [services.prismis-kind] in config.toml with api_key = "env:OPENROUTER_API_KEY", a timestamped backup of the previous file, no key value in any file it writes, and a second run that changes nothing.
README Quick Start, the .env template and the first-run text name OPENROUTER_API_KEY and match what the code reads.
After deploy, cerebro's daemon gets OPENROUTER_API_KEY from `apiconf env prismis` at launch, verify passes, and the first fetch cycle completes.
